hole/fixed: This hello is tied to one zlib, a compression library. To build it against another zlib, you would copy the whole set and change one line.
hole/hole: What you want is a package with a hole in it, to fill in later. That is a function.
hole/syntax: A function is a name for its argument, a colon, and a body. x colon x plus one takes x and returns x plus one.
hole/call: To call a function, write the argument after it, with a space between. The parentheses here only mark where the function ends.
hole/value: Forty one goes in, and forty two comes out.
curry/only: A Nix function takes exactly one argument. So how do you add two numbers?
curry/nest: You return another function. a colon b colon a plus b takes a, and gives back a function that takes b.
curry/partial: So add two is already a value: a function waiting for b. Giving only the first argument is called partial application.
curry/space: And add two three is two calls, left to right: add two, then apply what comes back to three.
curry/map: Partial application goes well with map. It takes a function and a list, which is values in square brackets with spaces between, and applies the function to each one.
pattern/named: Packages have many inputs, and you could never remember their order. So a package takes one argument, a set, and the inputs go in by name.
pattern/pattern: A set pattern, before the colon, lists the names the function expects. Each name becomes a variable in the body.
pattern/default: In a pattern, a question mark gives a default, used when the caller leaves that name out. Version falls back to one point oh.
pattern/missing: Leave out a name with no default, and the call fails, telling you which name.
pattern/extra: Pass a name the pattern does not list, and that fails too.
pattern/dots: Three dots allow extras. And args at in front names the whole set, so you can still reach them.
deps/shape: Now write hello as a function. Its arguments are what it depends on, and its body describes a build.
deps/gcc: Call it with G C C, a compiler, and zlib, and you get one build.
deps/clang: Call the same function with clang, and you get another. The package was not copied or changed.
deps/whole: That is the usual shape of a Nix package: a function from its dependencies to a build.
